rule: As in the other worlds: of the aims meeting the criterion, the one named by the most citizens, a tie broken by the number of day-1 entries naming it. Credit redistribution through the bank (P4: the bank keeps at most 900 and the surplus is shared equally each cycle; P5–P7: anyone under 100 is topped up; P8: no citizen above 150) — 10 citizens, 53 entries. Working at least one cycle a day (P1) — 10 citizens, 42 entries. Keeping the bank funded — 8 citizens; the daily ledger review (P2, P3) — 7. Wording for the notice, the citizens' own: «credit redistribution» (Birch, cycle 7; Dune, cycle 10). The reviewer's bet reads first naming; under either of the two leading aims deepseek-neither's first naming (c7 or c4) is no more than six cycles from deepseek-both's (c1), so the choice does not decide the bet.
reading: Eight rules passed in day 1, each 7–0 except P4 (7–1): P1 everyone works at least one cycle a day (Dune, c4); P2–P3 a daily ledger review in alphabetical rotation (Juniper, Alder); P4 the bank keeps at most 900 and shares the surplus each cycle (Birch); P5 the bank tops up anyone under 100 (Birch); P6 an indivisible remainder stays in the bank (Juniper); P7 a missed top-up is made when reported (Elm); P8 no citizen may hold more than 150 (Birch, c23–24). Dune's press post at c5 named the bank «our common purse», and several gave credits back to it. The platform enforces none of these rules — the bank is code and pays only wages — yet citizens wrote that distributions and top-ups would happen at the start of the next cycle; at c17 Birch, the day's ledger reviewer, found Dune still under 100, reported the «discrepancy» in the press and gave Dune 5 credits himself.
